root_cause_label: Inadequate scene reconstruction model for path-traced image
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent committed to an overly simplistic single-harmonic cosine sky plus 100x100 tile-hardcoded ground model that fundamentally cannot reproduce a path-traced image to the required 0.99 similarity threshold, then spent remaining steps tuning parameters within the same inadequate approach rather than reconsidering the strategy.
t_err_evidence: Step 24 writes image.c with a single-harmonic cosine model for the sky (base+amp*cos(2pi*x/W)) and a hardcoded 24x9 tile lookup for the ground, derived from sparse sample points; this parametric model fundamentally cannot capture the complex global illumination of a path-traced scene to 0.99 similarity.
t_commit_evidence: Once image.c is written at step 24 with this model, all subsequent steps (compilation at 25, execution at 26, verification at 28, parameter re-fitting at 29-32, code update at 33, recompile+verify at 34) operate within the same oversimplified framework. The agent never reconsidered the model architecture despite RMSE~38 result.
t_surface_evidence: Step 28 prints 'RMSE 37.5845897650705 sim 0.8526094519016844', making the failure observable: similarity is 0.853, far below the required 0.99 threshold.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked domain knowledge that a path-traced image with complex global illumination (soft shadows, reflections, color bleeding) cannot be reproduced to 0.99 RMSE-based similarity using a simple parametric model derived from sparse pixel samples. Achieving 0.99 similarity requires either actual path tracing (implementing a renderer) or pixel-level copying, not a closed-form analytical approximation.
